title: Remove k Equal Neighbours

concept.title: A stack of runs: letter and how often it repeats
body: Now you remove **`k` equal neighbouring letters** at once (not just two), again and again. Store the letters on the stack together with the **length of the current run**: pairs `(letter, count)`. A new letter equal to the top letter increases the top count; when the count reaches `k`, the whole run is removed (**pop**). A different letter starts a new pair `(letter, 1)`.

After a run is removed, the two neighbours of the removed part become neighbours, and the next letter is compared with the new top pair: if it is the same letter, it continues that run. This is what makes the stack of runs correct. The stack also keeps the memory small.

statement: Repeat the following step as long as possible: choose `k` equal letters that stand next to each other and remove them. Print the final word, or `empty` if no letter remains. The result does not depend on the order of the choices.
inputFormat: The second line has the word.

examples.note: Remove eee, then ccc, then bbb, then ddd: aa remains.

hints: Keep pairs (letter, count) on a stack.
If the new letter equals the top letter, add one to its count; remove the pair when the count reaches k.
Rebuild the word by repeating every letter as often as its count says.
